why: A gate that only asserts success cannot carry a known failure: it is either red forever, and then
disabled, or the failing cell is quietly dropped and the documentation keeps offering a broken route.
So each cell records the outcome we have MEASURED, and the gate fails on any difference in either
direction. A cell that starts passing is as much a failure here as one that starts failing, because
the documentation written around it is now wrong — and that is the moment to notice, not months later.

_why: Agreement with 'what was measured' means nothing unless the measuring tool is identified: a runner
image moving npm, or an unpinned Bun changing behaviour, would otherwise read as a KinetixUI
regression or fix when it is neither.
Each manager records the MAJORS its cells have actually been measured against, and --check fails
when it meets a major that is not in the list — i.e. one nobody has ever checked these expectations
against. It is a SET, not one version, because two environments legitimately differ: see pnpm below.
DELIBERATELY MAJOR-ONLY, AND PLEASE DO NOT 'TIGHTEN' IT TO EXACT VERSIONS. Patch and minor drift on
a hosted runner is constant, and a gate that goes red for a patch bump is a gate someone switches
off — which is the exact fate this whole design exists to avoid. A major is different: install
semantics really do change across one, which is why Yarn 1 and Yarn 4 are two separate cells here.
The exact version measured is printed on every run regardless, so drift stays visible before it
matters. Adding a major to a list means MEASURING it first; listing one unmeasured would be exactly
the verification inflation this file exists to prevent.

npm.note: Two patch versions of the same major, both measured and both passing: 10.9.4 in a review container and 10.9.9 on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (CI run 40506108993, 2026-10-27). Recorded because this is precisely the runner-image drift the comparison is major-only to tolerate — the set check passed on major 10 while the exact versions differed, which is the intended behaviour and not a near miss.

pnpm.note: Two majors, both measured, both passing. CI and a local checkout genuinely run different pnpm: `pnpm/action-setup` with no `version` input installs the repository's `packageManager` version (12.3.1), so that is what CI measures, while an ambient pnpm outside the repository is 10.28.0 — and pnpm 10+ self-switches to `packageManager` inside the repo, which is why `pnpm --version` differs by directory here. Recording only 10.28.0 would have made this gate fail every CI run on a major mismatch while every install outcome matched: red forever, for a reason that is not about this project. Measured 2026-10-27: install and execute both pass under 12.3.1, same as under 10.28.0.

yarn-berry.provenance: Measured by hand and NOT re-verified in this container: `yarn` on PATH can be only one of Yarn's two product lines, and this environment's network policy denies repo.yarnpkg.com. Both yarn-berry cells are optional and uncompared unless --yarn-berry=<path> supplies a binary.

bun.pin: Pinned in .github/workflows/ci.yml by sha256 bf8ccbfb2b0b80159e0f9a6d15c55317add8077534dbc6130a3edb52fccb395c (bun-v1.4.4/bun-linux-x64.zip, 51794595 bytes). Change the pin and this record together.

npx.note: The EXECUTE route for npm runs `npx`, which is a different executable from `npm` and can be resolved by PATH from a different installation. Recorded separately because recording only npm's version certified the wrong program: an execute cell could pass under an unmeasured npx major while this file said the major was measured. Measured 2026-10-28 in a review container at 10.9.4, alongside npm 10.9.4. If CI reports a different npx major, that is the gap this entry exists to surface.

bunx.note: The EXECUTE route for bun runs `bunx`. Same reasoning as npx, and this manager is where the defect was first demonstrated the hard way: the pinned Bun archive ships no `bunx` at all, and a workflow step asserting `bun --version` passed on a runner that had none. That was fixed in the workflow without fixing the same assumption here. Measured 2026-10-28 at 1.4.4, from the symlink the workflow creates beside the pinned binary.
bunx.pin: Not pinned independently: `bunx` is a symlink to the `bun` binary pinned by sha256 in ci.yml, and Bun dispatches on argv[0]. If that ever stops being true, this entry needs its own pin.

execute/yarn.note: Yarn Classic has no dlx. The script already treats that refusal as the expected outcome, so the cell passes while the command fails; /docs says so on the Yarn tab.

execute/yarn-berry.note: Only measured when --yarn-berry=<path> supplies a Berry binary, because `yarn` on PATH can be only one of Yarn's two product lines. Berry has dlx, so unlike Classic this one really passes.

install/yarn.reason: MEASURED IN CI 2026-10-28, run 40643580887 job 122667114143 (ubuntu-latest, yarn 1.22.22, no pre-existing Yarn state): recharts@3.10.1 declares react-is as a peer dependency and neither Yarn line installs a transitive peer, so a clean Yarn consumer TYPECHECKS and then fails its BUILD on '[vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "react-is" from .../node_modules/recharts/es6/util/ReactUtils.js'. The other three managers install the same packed tarball and pass, so this is the unmet peer and not a packaging defect.
install/yarn.fix: UNKNOWN, and the remedy this field used to state is WRONG — do not apply it. It read "Declare react-is as a dependency of @kinetixui/ui". There is no correct entry for that manifest: react-is predicates are major-locked to React in BOTH directions (React 19 renamed the element brand from Symbol(react.element) to Symbol(react.transitional.element), and react-is only recognises its own major's brand), while @kinetixui/ui's peer is react ">=18", which admits React 18 AND 19. Any fixed major would therefore be wrong for one of them, and wrong SILENTLY: the predicate returns false for a genuine Fragment, recharts drops Fragment-wrapped <Cell> children in findAllByType, and cell fills are lost with no error. Declaring it as a peer instead does not fix this cell either, because Yarn does not install a peer automatically — which is the failure being recorded here. The real remedy is consumer-side resolution and is an OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, not a one-line manifest edit. Source: scripts/adoption/react-is-agreement.mjs (PR #493), whose header states "@kinetixui/ui does not declare react-is and must not"; verified against packages/ui/package.json on main d5390810, which declares no react-is and peers only react/react-dom at ">=18". Corrected 2026-10-31. The earlier withdraw-and-restore of this cell's CAUSE is a separate matter and is unaffected; see `history`.
install/yarn.documented: apps/web/src/lib/pm-commands.ts YARN_NEEDS_REACT_IS, shown on the Yarn tab of every @kinetixui/ui install command, plus a callout on /docs/installation.
install/yarn.when_this_starts_passing: Settle the cause first. If this cell starts passing while the recorded cause is still unsettled, that is itself information: record what changed. Do NOT read this as waiting on a react-is entry in @kinetixui/ui — see `fix`: that remedy is wrong and must not be applied. Updating this file to expect pass also means removing the Yarn caveat from pm-commands.ts and the callout from /docs/installation in the same change.
install/yarn.history: This cell's recorded cause was WITHDRAWN and then RESTORED on 2026-10-28, and the round trip is worth keeping. The gate used to record only a pass/fail bit, so 'this cell failed' and 'this cell failed for the documented reason' were one fact. When the signature check was added, this review container produced a DIFFERENT failure — typecheck, 'error TS2307: Cannot find module '@kinetixui/ui'', because the copy Yarn Classic installed from the tarball had no dist/ — and the react-is description could not be confirmed from it. Rather than average the two, the container's diagnostic was recorded and CI was allowed to adjudicate: run 40643580887 went red, named the react-is build error, and settled which environment is representative. The container-local dist-absence has never reproduced anywhere else and is NOT a product claim; its six verified facts are in the master report §26.U.10.6, root cause unknown.
install/yarn.do_not: Do not widen expect_error to accept both the build-stage react-is error and the container-local typecheck error. A cell that matches any failure is a cell that verifies nothing, which is the defect the signature check exists to catch. If an environment produces a third failure, measure it and record it as its own fact.

install/yarn-berry.reason: the same missing react-is peer as install/yarn. Measured on Yarn 4.18.1 with nodeLinker: node-modules, so it is not a Plug'n'Play artefact and not a Classic quirk — both Yarn lines fail identically.
install/yarn-berry.also: Yarn 4 additionally refuses any version published in the last ~7 days (npmMinimalAgeGate), which the fixture sets to 0 so it tests our packaging rather than Yarn's clock.
install/yarn-berry.when_this_starts_passing: same as install/yarn — update both cells and the docs together.
install/yarn-berry.expect_error_unmeasured: No diagnostic is recorded for this cell because its failure has never been captured here: it is measured only when a Berry binary is supplied with --yarn-berry=<path>, and this container cannot install one (the network policy denies repo.yarnpkg.com). The gate now REFUSES a cell recorded as a known failure that carries no expect_error, so supplying a Berry binary will fail the run until someone measures the failure and records the diagnostic it actually prints. That refusal is deliberate: recording a signature nobody has observed is the verification inflation this file exists to prevent.
